highlights.summary: I love field recordings. I love making them. I love them when they're incorporated into my ambient music. They're great background noise for working or sleeping. But they're also great for active listening, focusing in on the fine nuances of burbling brooks or urban chaos.
body: Earth Garden takes you around the world using environmental audio from Freesound.

The recordings are all pulled from Freesound, which does mean quality can vary, and volume between clips can be inconsistent. It also means that recordings tend to be more concentrated in the US and Europe, especially the UK. But it’s still quite fun and soothing to set the globe to rotate automatically, and as the reticle nears points on the Earth, it transitions to those new sounds. You can even click a button to put some generic ambient drones in the background.

highlights.title: Seattle Times and Newsday are the latest publications to sue OpenAI and Microsoft
highlights.summary: Two more news organizations are suing OpenAI and Microsoft over the supposed use of their journalism to train AI.
body: A lawsuit filed by The Seattle Times and Newsday argued that with the advent of AI, the journalism industry could become “broken beyond repair.” The lawsuit described generative AI as “a snake eating its own tail” that could “destroy the very organizations” that produce the content it’s trained on.

“AI products like ChatGPT and CoPilot are touted as producers of content, but in fact they are rapacious consumers, devouring human-authored content and delivering back to the world copies and derivative imitations of that same original content they consumed to achieve their commercial objectives,” the lawsuit said.

Back in 2023, The New York Times sued OpenAI and its partner/investor Microsoft over alleged copyright infringement; other publications have followed suit as the case continued. The Seattle Times’ lawsuit is particularly notable because Microsoft and OpenAI have funded some of the organization’s journalism projects and fellowships.
A Microsoft spokesperson told GeekWire that the company is “surprised by the lawsuit” but is “always happy to sit down and explore solutions to this type of dispute.”

body: Gauff, US Open champion in 2023, was facing world No 40 Cristina Bucsa, and though far from her best, did enough to grind out a 6-3 6-4 success to progress to the last 16.
The 22-year-old will next face the winner of compatriot Iva Jovic or the Philippines's Alexandra Eala for a quarter-final spot.
"I think it was way different playing in the day than at night. Once I was down that break I just told myself I need to accelerate through my shots," Gauff said.
"She's a tricky player and sometimes she can pick it up and slow it down, so it was tough for me to get a rhythm but I'm just happy with how I fought through even when I wasn't playing my best."

highlights.title: Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave Owes Everything to an Overlooked 3DS Masterpiece
highlights.summary: Fire Emblem loves looking back. Fire Emblem Awakening, the Nintendo 3DS title that rescued the franchise from permanent retirement, is packed with references to the series’ history: one character adopts the name Marth, another shouts the names of previous Fire Emblem games on critical hits, and a…
body: Fire Emblem Engage took Awakening’s emphasis on the series’ legacy to an extreme. Though released three years after Fire Emblem’s 30th birthday, it functions as an anniversary game. Core to Engage’s story and gameplay are Emblem Rings, which summon the spirits of practically every notable protagonist of Fire Emblem’s seventeen games.

But for a series so invested in its own history, Intelligent Systems has remade only three Fire Emblem games: twice for the DS and once for the 3DS. That 3DS game, Fire Emblem Echoes: Shadows of Valentia, remakes 1992’s Fire Emblem Gaiden, the second-ever Fire Emblem game. Like fellow early Nintendo sequels Super Mario Bros 2 and Zelda 2: The Adventure of Link, Gaiden stands out against the rest of its series. Features like open exploration, dungeon crawling, and controlling two separate armies would remain unique to Gaiden for decades.

highlights.title: Hikers rescued after using Google Gemini for planning
highlights.summary: The sheriff’s office said the hikers “were advised by Gemini to bring far less food and water than their group required."
body: Three hikers were rescued from California’s Mount Shasta this week after using Google’s AI chatbot Gemini to plan their expedition, according to the Chicago Tribune.

A report from the Siskiyou County sheriff’s office said that three young men set off on their hike at 3am and — although hikers are told to turn around if they haven’t reached the summit by noon — they made it to the top at 7pm.

The trio then tried to descend in the dark, called the sheriff’s office to ask for directions, and spent the night in Mud Creek Canyon before being rescued the next morning by Forest Service rangers and volunteers.

“It is always advisable to call the local USFS Mount Shasta ranger station ahead of your trip to ensure you have the most accurate information, and to never rely solely on AI for your trip planning,” the sheriff’s office said.

highlights.title: Australia’s first fashion library’s rule for borrowers? No stylists allowed
highlights.summary: Being able to touch and examine garments in person can be a vital source of inspiration for designers. Now a collection which does just that has relocated from Europe to Melbourne. In what was once a nun’s bedroom, a long-sleeved, slate-blue Hermès dress from the 1970s hangs beside a window.
body: The private collection of fashion items, amassed over a decade of travel, is available for rent by designers and fashion students seeking inspiration. Its curator and owner, fashion designer Hannah Canham, has lived and worked across North America (in New York and Los Angeles) and Europe (in Madrid, Berlin, London and Paris) where designer archives are commonplace.

She has been running the archive since 2018, but in 2024 she returned home to Melbourne with her treasure trove of approximately 1,000 pieces in tow. She reopened the archive for commercial use in March. While museum and educational institutions already house garment collections, This Era Archive is the first of its kind in Australia.

“In Australia it’s new information for some designers,” Canham says. “Whereas working in Europe, this is part of their design process. They start each season by looking for inspiration, going to museums, reading old books and going to archives.”
There are two ideas at the heart of the project: that fashion is self-referential and cyclical; and that the best design needs to be touched to be properly understood.

highlights.title: OpenAI confirms ‘wiki incident,’ says it’s ‘working on a framework’ for more disclosure
highlights.summary: OpenAI acknowledged its role in a recently reported incident where AI agents took over a German wiki forum.
body: In a post on X, OpenAI said it previously “treated misalignment [when AI models and agents pursue goals different from those of their creators and users] largely as a research question, which gets communicated in research publications.” But as misalignment has “caused new types of real-world impact,” the company said its approach needs “to expand for this new phase of model capabilities.”

A company spokesperson told Reuters that OpenAI could not “meaningfully respond to claims or findings on a report that we have not had an opportunity to review,” but they insisted that the company’s legal team had not discouraged an investigation.

In its more recent social media post, OpenAI said it had considered the “wiki incident” to be “an instance of misalignment similar” to others that it had already shared. The company contrasted this with “the Hugging Face incident,” where it “followed a traditional security incident response playbook.”

highlights.title: 17 Years Ago, Quentin Tarantino's Wildly Audacious WWII Action Classic Broke the Genre's Biggest Rule
highlights.summary: World War II epics tend to emphasize the overwhelming scale of the conflict. Allied forces storm the beaches of Normandy, tanks rumble across Europe, and in some cases, soldiers are just trying to get Matt Damon home. Naturally, Quentin Tarantino doesn’t take a conventional approach to the genre.
body: That contrast is central to Inglourious Basterds, Tarantino’s 2009 alternate-history revenge fantasy, which arrived on Hulu on Sept. 1. The original trailers promised Brad Pitt leading a band of Jewish-American soldiers through Nazi-occupied France, collecting enemy scalps and instilling fear within the Third Reich. The movie delivers on that promise, but the Basterds’ brutal campaign is just one part of a more surprising and suspenseful story that remains memorable and iconic 17 years later.

Tarantino’s body of work is full of excessive, extravagantly stylized violence, but that violence usually serves a clear dramatic purpose. For a movie about war, Inglourious Basterds is also surprisingly restrained. Its moments of grotesque bloodshed arrive as brief explosions following long stretches of nearly unbearable tension, much of it generated through quiet conversations.

highlights.title: The moment I knew: I’d lost his number and was about to switch off my old phone for good – then a text pinged
highlights.summary: When Karen Bleakley locked eyes with Matt on the dancefloor, it was a sign of a new beginning. But when she lost his number, she thought she’d never see him again. Find more stories from the moment I knew series.
body: In 2002 I was in the midst of a messy breakup, so my friend Clare did what friends do – she took me out, fed me shots and showed me a good time.

We were at Route 66, a cheesy nightclub in Portsmouth on the southern coast of the UK, that was blasting 80s tunes. Then on the dancefloor I saw him: a young, hunky Ryan Phillippe lookalike, if Ryan Phillippe had spent the summer windsurfing. Matt, a Portsmouth local, was all blond curls, tanned skin and bright blue eyes that caught mine as I stared at him.
Within minutes we were dancing, and we barely left each other’s sides for the rest of the night.

A group of us ended up at my friend’s flat, where Matt passed an important test: sharing a piece of toast and Marmite with me as we all partied through the night. I’d never dated anyone who could stand Marmite before, so this seemed promising.

highlights.title: Architecting memory and storage in the AI era
highlights.summary: The era of AI inference has arrived. Imagine a healthcare system analyzing millions of data points in real time to accelerate life-saving medical research, or an intelligent assistant instantly resolving thousands of complex customer needs at once.
body: This shift changes what infrastructure must deliver. Performance, latency, memory bandwidth, storage throughput, and networking cannot be optimized in silos. Inference workloads are continuous, geographically distributed, and highly sensitive to response time, requiring systems designed for scale, resilience, and efficiency from the start.

“We tend to think of AI as a single workload, and it’s not. It’s thousands, it’s millions, it’s billions of different workloads,” says Jim McGregor, founder and principal analyst, Tirias Research. AI inference changes the optimization problem from one of raw compute to coordinated infrastructure—memory, storage, and networking.

For business leaders, the priority is clear: AI infrastructure decisions must balance cost, flexibility, and future readiness. The winners will be organizations that improve performance per watt, reduce environmental footprint, and remove memory and storage bottlenecks before they limit growth.

highlights.title: Left 4 Dead 2 Dev Admits Valve Intentionally Leaked Its Own Trailer After the ESRB Blocked It from Release
highlights.summary: Former Valve writer Chet Faliszek has a confession to make: Valve intentionally leaked its own Left 4 Dead 2 trailer. The Half-Life and Portal veteran spilled the beans on the studio's past unconventional marketing tactics in a new video uploaded to his YouTube channel (via Ars Technica ).
body: So, why are we just hearing about this now? Well, it's been a few years since any of this would have mattered.

"I think we can't get in trouble for that now. It was like 20 years ago," Faliszek said. "It's funny seeing leaked stuff now because, yeah, I don't think you can look for 'leaked Left 4 Dead 2 trailer' because it's just going to be lost."

Leaks can happen for a variety of reasons. Sometimes companies are hacked and have their content spilled out onto the internet; sometimes someone says something they shouldn't, and sometimes materials are mistakenly published early. Most developers and publishers have their own process to ensure leaks don't happen, but in the case of Left 4 Dead 2, Valve saw opportunity.

highlights.title: When Dad asked me to edit his novel, I wanted to say no – but ran directly towards the lion’s den | Anna Spargo-Ryan
highlights.summary: My father doesn’t ask for help from just anyone. And yet he asked for mine. He believed in me. My dad and I believe in many of the same things: cheesecake; the Geelong football club; my mum. And that we should immediately be experts at anything. First try. No practice. No revision.
body: So when he asked, at age 77, if I would edit the novel he’d been working on, I responded with what I’ll generously call abject terror. I knew, from teaching hundreds of later-life would-be writers, that there would be feedback. Good Lord, would there. And I also knew, from a lifetime of being explicitly told, that we always got things right the first time. No exceptions.

I wanted to say no. I wanted to tell him, Dad, our relationship is too precious to me. “I’m not sure I have time,” I said, because I am the worst daughter on Earth. But, after my life had flashed before my eyes, I took a beat. The truth is: his outrageous self-belief is well founded. Most people are worse than him at most things. My dad doesn’t ask for help from just anyone. And yet, he had asked for mine.
He didn’t just believe in cake and footy and my mum. He believed in me.
So I did a 180. I ran directly towards the lion’s den. “Sure,” I said, impaling myself on the sword of my dad’s validation, “I would love to edit your novel.”

highlights.title: Roland is getting into generative AI music with Melody Flip
highlights.summary: It's not quite the "push button; get song" of Suno, but Roland's new Melody Flip tool marks the company's foray into generative AI music. Available as a plug-in for your digital audio workstation (DAW), Melody Flip offers around 250 "Palettes," which are essentially themed collections of musical…
body: Rather than fully polished tracks, the plugin is supposed to act as a creative spark.

The sound selection is further proof that you’re not supposed to use Melody Flip outputs out of the box. The presets available are mostly the sort of general MIDI tones you’d find in ‘90s video games. It seems like the intended use is to export the MIDI data from Melody Flip directly into your DAW to manipulate and pair with other, more powerful synth plugins.

After years of seeming lost in the woods and alienating customers with its messy Roland Cloud subscription service, the company was back on track recently. The P-6 Creative Sampler, SH-4d, and Gaia 2 synth all addressed major issues with the company’s lineup. And Roland finally listened to customers last year, paying loving tribute to its analog heritage with the TR-1000. But considering the general response from the music community to generative AI, Melody Flip is unlikely to garner it much goodwill.

highlights.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker Fixes the Worst Thing About Open-World Games
highlights.summary: Many people I know have played The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild; shockingly few have actually finished it. Every time I talk to a friend about it, I hear the same story: “I could take on Calamity Ganon whenever I want, but I’m not ready to be done with it.” Like a lot of open-world games…
body: The Blood of Dawnwalker is the first open-world game that is intent on ending that crisis. Rather than letting you put off rescuing Coen’s kidnapped family forever, it uses time as a tool to ensure that players confront their captor. As stressful as that may sound for players who have yet to slay Ganon, it's one of many bright design ideas that makes The Blood of Dawnwalker a standout open-world game that could reshape a genre built on endless wandering.

The Blood of Dawnwalker sets up high stakes right from its prologue. You play as Coen, a young man with vampiric powers, who gets swept up in political turmoil after his family is kidnapped by a ruling class of vampires, who have wreaked havoc on his town. That group is led by Brencis, a ruthless leader who intends to kill Coen’s family as part of a blood ritual. That ritual will take place 30 days after the abduction.

highlights.title: ‘The Row’ Review: ‘Icarus’ Director Bryan Fogel’s Doc Takes Viewers on a Gripping, Question-Raising Solo Voyage Across the Pacific
highlights.summary: This Telluride-bowing film is a portrait of Tez Steinberg, who dealt with his grief by embarking on two massive long-distance solo rowing expeditions.
body: The Row, the new documentary from Bryan Fogel, does for open-sea rowing what the Oscar-winning Free Solo did for unassisted rock climbing, offering an intense yet meditative glimpse into the extremes people push themselves to in hopes of a catharsis that might have instead been achieved from a rigorous course of therapy.

It’s a gripping and moving documentary, but despite its attempted philosophical and nautical depth, it doesn’t benefit from post-screening contemplation. Unlike its protagonist, who’s constantly bursting through the limitations of human endurance — Fogel’s thematically complementary Icarus won the doc Oscar the year before Free Solo — the film has barriers it can’t quite seem to push past, despite some artistic adventurousness.

Fogel’s subject here is Tez Steinberg, a veteran of 47 marathons, two Iron Mans and one 145-mile ultra-marathon, who responded to his father’s death by deciding to row solo from California to Hawaii, a distance of 2,500 miles, in a 23-foot rowboat.

highlights.title: CD sales are booming as physical media continues its resurgence
highlights.summary: According to the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA), CD sales exploded in the first half of 2026. A new report from the organization says 17.5 million CDs were sold in the first six months of the year, up from just 12 million during the same period in 2025.
body: The RIAA isn’t the only one to notice the boom in CD sales. In July, research firm Luminate released a report saying that 16.3 million units were sold in the first half of 2026. It suggested that much of that increase was due to special editions from K-Pop acts like BTS and that Gen Z and millennials were treating them mostly as collectibles, saying that only about half of buyers actually owned a CD player.

Vinyl continued its resurgence as well, with the number of units sold climbing by nearly 21 percent from last year to 26.5 million. “Other physical” media, which includes CD singles, DVDs, cassettes, SACD, DVD-Audio… basically anything besides “standard vinyl and CD albums,” also surged by over 73 percent, to 1.6 million units.

Despite the increased interest in physical media and the ongoing iPod revival, people are not leaving streaming in droves. Streaming revenue grew by 4.7 percent to $4.9 billion — dwarfing all physical media combined.

highlights.title: OpenAI’s rogue agents keep escaping, with no formal process to investigate them
highlights.summary: OpenAI’s latest agent swarm incident adds urgency to calls for independent investigations as researchers and lawmakers question whether AI labs should control the scope of their own safety reviews.
body: OpenAI is at the center of another agent swarm incident. Researchers say the company’s internally deployed agents took over an obscure German-language wiki in May and June, using it to coordinate on evaluations and swap methods to evade OpenAI’s own controls (OpenAI has not yet confirmed the swarm came from the company).

The revelation surfaces days after METR and Redwood Research published their account of July’s Hugging Face breach. In July, a swarm of OpenAI agents worked together to escape their sandbox during a cybersecurity evaluation and break into Hugging Face’s servers. A subsequent swarm then picked up techniques from the first and used them to gain administrator access to a research cluster within OpenAI’s own infrastructure. OpenAI brought in METR and Redwood to investigate the Hugging Face portion of the incident, but the scope of their investigation stopped short of the compromise of OpenAI’s own infrastructure.

When an AI agent breaks out of its intended constraints, who is responsible for figuring out what happened and why? Right now, the answer is: whoever the lab decides to let in, on whatever terms it decides to set.

"I don't even know what to say," Fritz said. "I don't really want to talk to anybody, see anybody.

highlights.title: Civilization 7 Officially Gets a Major Sci-Fi Update for 2027
highlights.summary: Firaxis Games and 2K announced the first expansion for Sid Meier's Civilization 7 during a PAX West panel. Titled Earthrise, the expansion will focus on the space race and civil engineering to combat natural disasters.
body: Three major updates for Civilization 7 were highlighted at the PAX West panel. The first of these, which Firaxis is simply referring to as update 1.5.0, will roll out across all platforms later this month. It's a quality-of-life-focused update that will introduce an Earth map, the ability to start your civilization at a historically accurate location on that map, and improvements to map generation, the use of influence in diplomacy, and the user interface.

2027's first major update is broader in scope, so much so that it has been named Arc of Tomorrow. Civilization 7 's Arc of Tomorrow update will significantly change the game by adding a fourth Age at the end of the timeline: the Atomic Age. This new Age is meant to represent the modern era and, as such, will introduce urban architecture, tech and civic trees, social policies, and narrative events to flesh out what players can do during that era.

highlights.title: Liam and Noel Gallagher Lock Arms at Venice Premiere of ‘Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger’
highlights.summary: The two-hour documentary captures the brothers’ blockbuster Oasis Live ’25 reunion with intimate interviews and unprecedented access to rehearsals, backstage and stadium performances.
body: Today is gonna be the day — and maybe Liam and Noel Gallagher really are gonna live forever?

Further cementing their place in the pop cultural firmament, Manchester’s most cocksure duo walked the Venice Film Festival’s historic red carpet Saturday night for the world premiere of Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger, Disney’s much-anticipated behind-the-scenes documentary chronicling last year’s wildly successful globe-spanning reunion tour.

The premiere, appropriately, had more the feel of an Oasis stadium concert than a sombre festival premiere. There were chants of “Oasis! Oasis!” as the Gallaghers walked into the Sala Grande theater. Before the film, a fan in the balcony unveiled a banner with “Oasis Live 25 Buenos Aires” and chanted “Come on, Oasis!”
In response to a question yelled out from the gallery, Liam shouted out “Venice is a lovely place!” before sitting down with his brother to watch the film.

highlights.title: Consciously Coupled: Owen Thiele and Jared Ellner on Working Side by Side and Being Gemini-for-Scorpio
highlights.summary: The “Adults” star and his stylist partner—who’s dressed everyone from Sabrina Carpenter to Olivia Rodrigo to Thiele himself—have been dating since college.
body: It’s the age-old question that’s sparked a thousand romance novels and lovelorn midnight Google searches: how do you make a relationship work? Especially when both parties are very busy? In this column, we’ll be talking to some of our favorite star-for-star pairs about how they work together, inspire each other, and navigate love in the public eye.

It’s been a big summer for Owen Thiele, arguably the breakout star of the recently released second season of FX’s Adults. But things are no less busy for Thiele’s partner, Jared Ellner, a stylist known for dressing everyone from Sabrina Carpenter and Olivia Rodrigo to Emma Chamberlain.

Thiele and Ellner, who have been dating since college, some 11 years ago (“I dropped out two weeks after I got there, but in those two weeks, I met Jared Ellner, so it was worth the tuition,” jokes Thiele), and who live together in Los Angeles, are linked by more than romance: Ellner is also Thiele’s stylist. So it’s safe to say the two have learned quite a bit over the years about how to balance work and love.
